items.body: Palagoma is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. Odd Okoddo, the duo of Kacirek and Ratengo, has been performing since 2018, but with the inclusion of the 83 year old Nengo, a singer from the eastern part of the country, there�s an added traditional depth to the music. A 2025 performance shows Nengo�s lifetime of experience singing Kenya�s dodo tradition around 2 and half minutes in (see below). Furthermore, her inclusion on this album allows her and Ratengo to toss the vocals back and forth as they reference their shared roots (Ratengo and Nengo live minutes from each other). Musically, however, the tracks are driven by Kacirek�s Buchla synth, hand percussion, and occasional kit drumming, which serve to buoy the voices without blotting out the music�s origins. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Bara,� for example, begins with the dime-store thwack of a repeated pattern, a stiff juxtaposition to the voices; yet, as the song rolls along, a 4/4 clink appears, then a burbling bass, and finally, what sounds like a xylophone. Layers of synthesized polyrhythms keep presenting themselves with a subtlety almost unnoticeable, until, by the track�s end, it feels organic, as if it�s all been underneath the two voices all along. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Sarah,� perhaps the album�s most intense track, features a lead vocal from Ratengo and tentative, percussive spittles from Kacirek. And while the technology never tries to overtake the vocals, it does sneak up and punctuate the track�s urgency, as edgy distortion sneaks in here and there just as Ratengo�s voice reaches its peak. The term �folktronica� has been bandied about as a way to house the type of music on offer here. In fact, exploratory collaborations such as Chouk Bwa & The �ngstr�mers as well as much of Kampala, Uganda�s Nyege Nyege label house sounds that might be �folktronic� in some way. What�s more interesting and important about this music, though, is how truly global so much of it is while maintaining a deep connection to Africa and its diasporic communities. The music on Palagoma , as well as much of what�s linked above (and available in countless other recent recordings) demonstrates a real willingness for cultures to respond to each other without trampling traditions altogether. Instead, roots become avant-garde and innovations become seemingly thousands of years old. Certainly the inclusion of an 83 year old traditional Kenyan singer only recently making her global debut as she tours with a duo whose instrumental voice is a white male saturated in electronic Kenyan rhythms demonstrates this blurring. The music this trio makes is certainly of the 21st century, but it�s often hazy, sparse, and open, keeping it from a quick sell-by date or confining it to a specific genre. Instead, it�s a beautiful example music as grace.

items.artist: Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy
items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,

is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 乐队的这张专辑延续了首张作品的杂糅风格，所有演奏乐器均由废旧物品手工制作，包括被命名为 tassofons、kitchenofon 等的自制乐器。评论指出这些自制乐器的音准精度出乎意料，在现代录音环境下呈现出丰富饱满的音质。曲目涵盖了多种世界音乐风格：以单簧管领奏的克莱兹默曲调、库姆比亚风格的西班牙合唱与拉丁打击乐、非洲节拍灵感下的木鱼与沙锤配马林巴琴旋律、桑巴节奏的横笛段落，以及带有中东迷幻色彩的长笛旋律。乐手在各曲目中展现出即兴演奏能力，融合了爵士化的技巧处理。整张专辑以幽默而独特的方式呈现跨文化音乐对话，强调音乐人对节奏、旋律与和声的普世追求，同时反思了商业乐器过剩与音乐本质之间的关系。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家 Omar Sosa 在意大利 Fazioli 钢琴厅进行了一场两小时的独奏即兴录音，后经后期制作加入人声采样、打击乐、循环音、野外录音和环境音效等元素。专辑诞生于2021年疫情封锁期间，创作者经历了婚姻变故，在米兰演出取消后被邀请至这家以古典钢琴传统著称的厂牌录音。Sosa 强调即兴创作中'没有错误的音符'，推崇首遍录制的自然状态，融汇爵士、拉丁、古典等多种传统却不囿于任何类型标签。他在采访中谈及对算法时代音乐分类的抵触，倡导'少即是多'的哲学理念，主张音乐应超越市场分类的局限，触及人类共同的精神体验。专辑开场曲展示了从键盘延伸至琴弦内部的演奏手法，让乐器本身的共鸣体成为创作素材。

items.body: Untitled brings a form of fantasy music where society or environment is imagined in an advanced technological and scientific age exploring the universe, time, future tech, and humanity. The monstrous and crazy hypnotic repetitive sound is the art of the impossible, famously indistinguishable from magic, a way to test new ideas and take tomorrow. Everyone is here riding into the unknown Untitled by RGL   The sound of strange science fiction dreams and dramas creating whole universes of the mind, with mutant ambient guitars, synths and beats, Untitled showcases a wide-ranging sonic palette, such as abstract drones placed alongside rhythm-driven tracks, modern electronic music that explores deep philosophical and psychological themes, encouraging the constant listener to contemplate the kind of future that waits somewhere ahead. If we don’t innovate, something else will. Untitled brings a form of fantasy music where society or environment is imagined in an advanced technological and scientific age exploring the universe, time, future tech, and humanity. The monstrous and crazy hypnotic repetitive sound is the art of the impossible, famously indistinguishable from magic, a way to test new ideas and take tomorrow. Let’s get started. The opening track is “I” (2:45). I imagine a twisted clock with sparks flying, heavy echo, busy guitar clockwork and pulsing electronic splashes. We are heading out into the unknown, with no name. Traveling like this distorts time, the sunrise starts again, “II” (3:48). Once the beat starts the sense of motion pushes ahead. I see endless fields and the electronic drone, with visitors speeding over the rising haze of sunrise, endless flickering misty tall grass fields. We move on, into the swirling darkness. A hidden orchestra warms up slowly, one or two at a time, then more join in becoming a slow imperceptible development of the environment and atmosphere, “III” (4:44) is like a sun bath, just sit and enjoy. “IV” (6:28) has a mysterious opening, entering into a dark Funhouse, a nervous fast beat shadowed by drones and other strange things, with voices somewhere else, it is impossible to hear people talking, but there are clues. Perhaps now we are riding next to the engine, things start purring as if under the rhythm of the rails, feel the power, steady and sure. The forward motion starts again with “V” (5:23), a strange wet munching beat, bobbing in the void with others, we are not alone and they are hungry. There is also a flute, which fits in an odd twisting solo over the strange wet sloshy beat that chews along at a slow and dangerous pace. I see distant embers glowing at night :: “VI” (4:34) starts with the sound of wet rocks, or perhaps the surface of a large body of water when it is very quiet, I don’t know. Maybe I see distant embers glowing at night, an old campfire by a new lake, more new things come and go but the main thing is the pattern itself. There is a huge rainbow glow in the sky which dominates the imagination. Next, on “VII” (3:18), the call goes out. The darkness is thick. The drone of the searchlight as it reaches into the inky blackness covers the visiting Martian judges, who are mumbling quietly amongst themselves. For the final séance the beats pick up as we go along into the end of it all, “VIII” (5:04). Opening into a frosty sparkling shimmering sunrise, phantom drones sustain throughout. Soon a beat bangs into form, abruptly kicking and tapping, the rhythmic machine builds and builds. The force stays strong, the elements shift and fit into new forms, bringing a host of wanderers. Everyone is here riding into the unknown. RGL is a Tokyo-based producer known for his lo-fi house productions and analog-textured dance music, with releases on labels such as Diskotopia and Breaker Breaker. In 2025, he released his debut album, Touzan. He is a member of the producer collective COSMOPOLYPHONIC and co-hosts the radio program COOL RADIO with fellow collective member RLP. The result is a work that crystallizes RGL’s distinctive sensitivity to sound and texture. Untitled is available on ato.archives. items._cn_summary: RGL的《Untitled》是一部以科幻叙事为骨架的实验电子作品，融合了变形的吉他音色、合成器纹理与节奏脉冲。专辑以罗马数字编号的六首曲目展开，从迷幻的钟摆意象到黑暗游乐园般的声景，再到湿润的节奏律动，乐评以视觉化的语言描绘每一曲的听觉体验，将听众带入一个探索宇宙、时间与人类未来的未知空间。整体手法强调氛围构建与重复催眠式的节奏结构，跨越ambient、drone与rhythmic electronic之间，既有静态冥想的段落，也有推进感强烈的节拍驱动作曲，呈现出多层次的声响实验特质。

items.body: Hana Stretton’s album tiarn is filled with the kind of hazy lo-fi arrangements that pull on the heart strings of sepia toned memories, fading Polaroid snapshots in sound of private moments and community life alike. It’s not crazy to learn that some old family camera footage is part of the inspiration behind these songs. A seduction to enter into, like sleep itself tiarn by Hana Stretton   Hana Stretton’s tiarn is an exercise in dream reverie and hypnagogic songcraft. It’s a twilight album set between the edge of waking and sleep, night and day. It’s soft cadences are like the allure of the ocean, a seduction to enter into, like sleep itself, it catches you unaware and before you know it, you are inside another world with its own rules, its own logic. The pieces for this, her sophomore effort, were crafted during a period of time while living quite alone near the Pacific Ocean on its Australian shores. It was her habit to go down to the water and swim in the blue of dusk. These azure dips overlapped with the winter whale migrations, and perhaps some of their songs seeped into her own mind and soul. Water keeps things in the flow and ideas for music swam into her during her ritualistic purifications in the icy salt water. On the walk back home the melodies would surface and she would record these as the evening progressed. It’s this naturalistic process that gives the album its striking yet elusive character. Ideas for songs, poems or stories can come in a flash and they can come strongly, but they slip away just as easily. Paying close attention to them by the constant humming, constant singing, constant courting of the songs that wish to emerge is no easy to task, but Stretton has managed to coax these pieces out of that creative borderland, where there is always the risk of them slipping away, and into this suite of recordings that have made them very much alive. Stretton was born in Canberra, Australia, between Sydney and Melbourne. Permaculture, that mighty gift of ecological philosophy given to world by David Holmgren and Bill Mollison was born in Tasmania. One of my favorite principles from permaculture is the idea to “use edges and value the marginal.” It’s on the margins where different kinds of ecological systems blend together. It’s in the margins where different kinds of musical genres blend together. Here those genres are ambient and folk music, creating an idiosyncratic lo-fi blend. Her inspiration, as noted before also came from the margins of ocean and land, and it’s this dreamy characteristic between waking and sleep I find so pervasive across these wonderful pieces.   Bits of environmental detritus permeate the arrangements which consist of strings, pipes, synth, what sometimes sounds like accordion, many things I cannot make out exactly because of the way they are mixed maximalizes a sense of immateriality. Whiffs of field recordings, captured conversation, rain or wind throughout. The art of field recording reverses itself :: Field recording is now a folk art. Not only in the sense that the great ballad preservers of the past such as John and Alan Lomax went out into the field with reel-to-reels to record folk songs, but now, when most anyone can record environmental sounds on the fly, field recordings of the ambience of everyday life. That’s when the art of field recording reverses itself once again from being something that had once been used to preserve vanishing ways of folk life to becoming a folk art in itself. Hana Stretton’s album tiarn is filled with the kind of hazy lo-fi arrangements that pull on the heart strings of sepia toned memories, fading Polaroid snapshots in sound of private moments and community life alike. It’s not crazy to learn that some old family camera footage is part of the inspiration behind these songs. Before she was born her family had lived in Japan in the ‘90s. A young family looks over valleys to the mountains beyond during the summer. Her parents had also bought a synthesizer they never used while in Tokyo. She started using that synth and it was a way to reconnect to the past. Some of the sounds from the camera footage also make up the field recordings that were used—the hushed conversations, the rain, the wind, insects buzzing. This is the place where family tapes and home movies form another kind of private documentary, a documentary now shared in all its vulnerability. “Yet I know these soundscapes and songs were composed even if it feels as if when I am listening, that I am just caught up inside of Stretton’s daydream. It’s not a bad daydream to be inside of, especially on a lazy afternoon” ~Justin Patrick Moore Isolationist piano tinkles meet lazily strummed, half strummed, barely strummed, guitars and other instruments that just seem to fall out of the speakers effortless. Yet I know these soundscapes and songs were composed even if it feels as if when I am listening, that I am just caught up inside of Stretton’s daydream. It’s not a bad daydream to be inside of, especially on a lazy afternoon. The group singing of the choir who collaborated with her on the song “As It Was Before This” is one of the points on the record where the tension between the individual and community is felt. The choir is reminiscent of heavenly realms and oceanic expanses. A sense of communion with powers outside the self is heard through these uplifting voices as they bridge material and non-physical realms. This feels like a very private album, very personal in its overall vision, aesthetic and design, yet I hear a longing for connection in these songs. Other players are here as well, other voices. Yet the mingle in with her own playing, her own compositions. The word tiarn means landholder. Stretton shows her ability on this record to be a songholder bridging the realms of ocean and land, dream and waking life, bringing back treasures from the deep to share with the world. tiarn was released independently in August, with vinyl editions through P.W. items.body: Friendship Survival Guide arrives as a blessing and a gift. In many ways we are still mourning the loss of Jóhann Jóhannsson, as his music is woven into the fabric of our lives. In the eight ensuing years, a few posthumous recordings have been released, along with a pair of box sets collecting his oeuvre; but the composer’s voice has been mostly silent since then. Enter close friend Adam Wiltzie, who earlier had collaborated with Jóhannsson on the scores for The Theory of Everything and Arrival. Wiltzie had held onto the analog tape loops from these sessions and later recorded guitars under the guidance of Steve Albini before Albini’s own passing, adding an extra layer of urgent melancholy. Friendship Survival Guide is an elegiac statement, approved by Jóhannsson’s family, that is not as much about surviving a friendship as it is about the experience of losing a friend. Wiltzie honors Jóhannsson while extending his legacy, completing an “artifact they created together” and offering it to the world in hopes that the healing might continue. As one might expect from the co-founder of Stars of the Lid, the music is as much ambient as modern composition, a melding of disciplines that forms a harmonious whole. The poignant “September Nineteen Sixty Nine” leads off the set; in this month, both composers were born but two days apart. The opening notes are like a lift-off, the launching of a life; in this case, two lives that would eventually intertwine. Immediately one is impressed by the brass and strings, the stately drama, the grand chords, surging first to one peak and then another. In less than three minutes, Wiltzie encapsulates all of his friend’s astonishing talents. The two-part “Dazed and Reflective Glory” introduces an abrasion of notes, like fading memories, corroded tapes, sheet music nibbled by moths. This abrasion fades in the second half as clearer, more insistent notes shine through, as if to suggest that time will not decorate this memory with rust. Every time the notes fade, we fear it will be the last, but we have learned otherwise. When the gentle choir begins to sing on “Mourners Will Be Outcast,” one thinks less of a funeral service than of an ascension, with new compositions wafting through the ether, descending through the clouds, borne on the mist and dew. Even as the choir recedes, the organ continues to play. Forboding clouds gather in “Exceptional Proportions,” threatening a deluge that thankfully does not occur. Instead there lies tenderness and hope in the nourishing rain of “Give Into Gravity.” The piece is an invitation to incorporate grief with its worthy companion, gratitude, and never to allow the first to walk alone. The choir returns like the acknowledgment of a prayer. The first single, “White Gloves & Turtlenecks,” is also the album’s shortest piece; and contains the album’s most overt violin melody, like a voice cutting through the fog. The track is matched with a video: the first part of a continuing story, promising more. In contrast, “Soft Favourites” is by far the album’s longest and most ambient piece, a soft reflection like a walk home from the chapel in slowly-falling snow. Midway through the piece, new chords emerge like visitations. The stars are twinkling, sending messages of their own. The title “In Ever Decreasing Circles” suggests fate closing in, the inevitable weight of time. Echo and breath populate the composition, along with some surprising glissandos that recall the score for Arrival. Yet this is only fitting, as a fine line exists between science and science fiction, just as there does between faith and fact. “Where You Are Now, Voyager” offers a clever play on words, referring not only to Voyager and its famed golden disc, but to the notes of a beloved composer, echoing through time; and to Jóhannsson himself, a voyager lost to us physically, but spiritually present, made all the more real through this exquisite resurrection of sound. (Richard Allen) Available here

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Adam Wiltzie对已故好友Jóhann Jóhannsson的致敬之作。Wiltzie保留了早年两人为《万物理论》和《降临》配乐时合作的模拟磁带循环片段，并在录音师Steve Albini指导下录制了吉他部分。整张专辑以环境音乐与现代作曲的融合为基调，铜管、弦乐与合唱交织成庄严的戏剧性结构。开场曲'1969年9月'以升腾般的音符象征两个生命的交织；'Dazed and Reflective Glory'两部分呈现模糊记忆与清晰音符的对话；合唱在'Mourners Will Be Outcast'中带来升天般的意境；'Give Into Gravity'则将悲伤与感恩融为一体。专辑不仅是悼念之作，更是对友谊与合作遗产的延伸与完成。

items.body: Goetia is a Turkish band I hadn’t heard of before. I discovered that they have released four singles since last year and are now launching their debut album, “Saligia”, featuring seven tracks -dealing with the 7 deadly sins. Incidentally, the four previously released singles are also included on the album. Their influences clearly lie within the broad realm of EBM. While the tracks remain rudimentary and minimal in their composition, some feature appealing, icy sounds. This is a fine example of a band getting the absolute most out of limited resources. The best proof of this is the track “Haris”, which stands out significantly and packs more punch than the other songs. Another distinctive feature of the production is that the vocals are delivered in their native language, with the exception of one German passage. Goetia certainly still has some work to do when it comes to the overall mix and production, but “Saligia” already sounds quite good and, above all, promising. I look forward to seeing what comes next. (Rating:7). Listen to “Haris”: Haris by Goetia About Goetia Goetia is a darkwave band based in Ankara, Türkiye, working around themes of occultism, inner conflict, and existential decay. The band combines darkwave, EBM, and industrial elements into a cold, immersive sound built on hypnotic rhythms, analog-inspired synthesizers, and minimal structures. Music and production on the group’s material are credited to Berent Oral and Tolgahan Pehlivanlı, with Pehlivanlı also handling lyrics, vocals, and mixing. A founding date has not been confirmed. Goetia released four singles ahead of its debut album: “Esans”, “Nihil”, “Döngü”, and “Nektar”. The band’s debut full-length, “Saligia”, followed on April 3, 2026 through Tamar Records. The title is a Latin acronym for the seven deadly sins (Superbia, Avaritia, Luxuria, Invidia, Gula, Ira, Acedia), and the seven-track album is built around that theme, with mastering by Uğur Yelkenci and cover artwork by Nuryağmur Candar.

items._cn_summary: Goetia 是一支来自土耳其安卡拉的暗潮乐队，首张专辑《Saligia》以七宗罪为主题，收录七首作品。乐队将暗潮、EBM 与工业元素融合，营造出冰冷的沉浸感，依赖催眠式节奏、模拟合成器音色与极简结构展开表达。主唱使用土耳其语演唱，仅有一段德语段落，形成了鲜明的地域语言特征。整体制作尚显粗砺，混音环节存在改进空间，但凭借有限的制作资源依然达成了不错的听感。其中《Haris》是专辑中最具冲击力的一首，力道明显超出其他曲目。专辑由 Tamar Records 独立发行，母带与封面设计亦体现了地下制作脉络。这是一张有潜力但仍处于成长阶段的暗潮作品，地域文化视角与母语演唱是其不可忽视的辨识度来源。

items.body: There exists a certain species of electronic music that has been embalmed by its own admirers, preserved beneath enough black clothing, antique drum machines, and solemn references to 1981 that you half expect the Smithsonian to issue the next twelve-inch. Mercury Girl’s latest single Spirit Forward escapes that mausoleum because Aaron Pena sounds less interested in curating the past than in using its machinery to pick a fight with the present. Pena, the Filipino American San Diego musician behind Mercury Girl, works with the familiar furniture of cold wave: stiff percussion, bass lines that keep walking even when the room feels empty, synthesizers that seem permanently one bad voltage spike away from collapse. Spirit Forward, however, has a wiry nervous energy that puts it somewhere between Black Marble’s private unease, the laboratory pop of Oppenheimer Analysis, Tom Vek’s angular minimalism, and the sideways rhythmic intelligence of Talking Heads. The bass carries most of the physical argument, a rubbery little engine repeating itself beneath chords that keep looking upward as though expecting an answer from a ceiling full of dead fluorescent tubes. The question is the oldest one available: “What’s the meaning of all of this?” Pena understands that asking it in 2026 means pushing through advertising, algorithms, compulsory self-branding, endless feeds, and the faint suspicion that somebody has already converted your existential crisis into a subscription tier. Its beat suggests motion without destination, which turns out to be a useful musical equivalent for living inside a culture forever promising connection while quietly perfecting isolation. “This song mirrors the frustrations I, and I’m sure many others, have had when trying to make sense of life and the meaning behind it, especially in a world so enveloped with distracting you from doing so,” says Pena. “We’re all fed ideas about who and what we should be; this song rejects those expectations.” Pena recorded the material with vintage synthesizers and half-working sequencers, and you can hear the appeal of equipment that misbehaves, because human uncertainty sounds better when the machines possess a little uncertainty of their own. The arrangement has space, but never comfort; every open patch seems to leave another philosophical bill unpaid. Listen to Spirit Forward below and order the single here. Spirit Forward by Mercury Girl Ahead of Mercury Girl’s debut album, A NuTone, Spirit Forward makes a persuasive case for Pena as a songwriter who understands that cold wave can still carry blood, doubt, humour, and the embarrassing human need to ask enormous questions while the drum machine keeps perfect time. items._genre: coldwave / post-punk / synth-driven electronic
items._cn_summary: Mercury Girl 第二支单曲《Spirit Forward》以冷波为骨架，却在惯性中寻求当下性。编曲沿用僵直的打击、行走贝斯与近乎失稳的老式合成器，却以紧绷的神经能量区别于纯粹的复古复刻。低频是全曲的支点——一段富有弹性的循环在仰望的和弦下方反复推进；鼓机营造出无目的的运动感，隐喻当代社会承诺连接却不断生产孤立的悖论。Pena 将录制中设备的偶然失灵视为一种审美资源：人自身的犹疑与机器的犹疑被并置，赋予合成器序列天然的呼吸。全曲提出一个古老的疑问——意义何在——并试图在算法、订阅、强制自我品牌的噪音中撕开一个缝隙。整体留有空间却不提供安慰，哲学账单始终悬而未决。

items._cn_summary: 这张1979年现场录音由Oregon乐队录制，融合了原声爵士、古典与世界音乐元素，形成独特的跨文化即兴风格。乐队以多变的成员构成和长久的创作生命力著称，演奏中吉他手Ralph Towner与各成员通过细腻的声部交织，营造出静谧而庄严的听觉空间。专辑记录了魁北克与纽约两地的现场演出，强调即兴对话与多层结构的世界观，展现出不拘一格的器乐组合方式。音乐在融合古典底蕴与民族素材的同时，也具备前卫爵士的探索精神，是该乐队长期风格脉络中的一枚重要现场见证。

items.body: Salt og Vind (Salt and Wind) comes from Norway’s Pjusk, aka Jostein Dahl Gjelsvik. Arriving after an eight-year break, Salt og Vind is also Pjusk’s first solo outing. The record details the forces of nature and its contrasting mood swings, from the violent to the calm, the at-ease to the tempest, but the music also contains a very human struggle – maybe an abject failure – to latch onto the eternal and instead seek out temporary pleasures. The longer pieces counteract the lapsing attention spans of life in 2022, and the slower pace leaves behind a sense of lasting fulfilment. The difference is night and day. Pjusk’s fourth album for 12k is stark and remains low in temperature. The rhythms are cold to the touch, emerging from the ice and splintering like a webbing of frost. Looking beyond nature, there’s a sense of the infinite and the finite, one presiding over the other, the immortal standing tall over the mortal, still in existence even as the other falls. Although elemental, the atmospheric ambient carries something of the spiritual and the philosophical. Recurring harmonies are buried deep in the mix, rolling in the dense, clouded textures. It stings and whips up the breeze, and the notes present slightly clearer images among its fog-coated, autumnal surroundings. The electronic tones are like age-old lifeforms with deeply-embedded survival instincts, able to go through anything and come out on the other side. Salt og Vind by Pjusk Making another long-anticipated return to the 12k label is Poland’s Tomasz Bednarczyk. Windy Weather Always Makes Me Think Of You features a collection of sounds recorded via a smartphone Dictaphone and a Sony field recorder. Taken over the last ten years, Tomasz’s goal was to ‘transform all gathered recordings into new, multi-layered harmonies’. The field recordings were taken from all over the world, and in their original state, the melodies were laced with environmental and elemental sounds. From those brief sounds, new harmonies have been reworked and revealed. With minimalism and subtle ambient variation at its heart, Windy Weather Always Makes Me Think Of You is slim in its emotional delivery and fragile in its chosen timbre, but its harmonies are towers of majesty and there is great power in its humility. Changes occur on a microscopic level; they’re indistinguishable from one day to the next, but they are there, slowly evolving and reshaping its notes and its identity. It is a slow-burning, expansive and powerful record, despite its fragmented origins (or perhaps because of them), rising up in spite of difficult beginnings and hardships, and the music is quietly moving. Things have not been easy, even with the natural world sitting at the centre of its music. Its expansive sound is mostly down to its association with the natural environment, and Tomasz is able to further channel the outdoors through the undulating, serene notes and the pulsing deeper textures that seem to thrum with life. Like the rest of 12k’s discography, there is a strong attention to detail. Every tone matters, from the skipping notes on ‘Underwater Kalimba’, the soft nocturnal dissolving of ‘Playing Stairs’, or the lilting, tropical ambient of ‘Somewhere In Hawaii’. If something is built on rocky foundations, it will fall, and Tomasz’s original recordings are strong enough to split themselves into new and original pieces. Windy Weather Always Makes Me Think Of You by Tomasz Bednarczyk www.12kmusic.bandcamp.com
items._genre: ambient / field recording / drone / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张12k厂牌合辑介绍了两位艺术家的作品。挪威音乐人Pjusk的《Salt og Vind》以冰冷的节奏和稀疏的和声描绘自然力量的暴力与宁静，长篇作品对抗当代碎片化的注意力。波兰音乐人Tomasz Bednarczyk的《Windy Weather Always Makes Me Think Of You》基于十年间用智能手机和录音机在全球采集的田野录音，将其转化为多层和声，以极简手法展现自然的广阔与脆弱。两张专辑均以自然为核心，但前者偏向氛围电子与哲学沉思，后者侧重田野录音与声音转化，在缓慢演变中构建深邃的听觉空间。

items.album: Pantheon
items.excerpt: Pantheon is a visual and immersive experience. Bon – a production, composition, writing, and art partnership between Yerosha Windrich and Alex Morris – are curious to go beyond, displaying an interest which borders on passion for all things relating to popular culture, nature, philosophy, and standardized, accepted perceptions. In that respect, Pantheon’s music is a mirror, looking directly back upon their own perceptions and philosophies on inclusivity, respect, and personal sovereignty.
items.body: Pantheon is a visual and immersive experience. Bon – a production, composition, writing, and art partnership between Yerosha Windrich and Alex Morris – are curious to go beyond, displaying an interest which borders on passion for all things relating to popular culture, nature, philosophy, and standardized, accepted perceptions. In that respect, Pantheon’s music is a mirror, looking directly back upon their own perceptions and philosophies on inclusivity, respect, and personal sovereignty. While the pair have UK roots, both come from mixed-race heritage, and as a result, Bon take a deeper look at counterculture and ‘the perception of what music means and stands for in society’. Their thoughtful, nature-oriented approach is a natural thing, too, as BON have always thought of their musical releases as being seasonal. Everything has its season and its time; the music burns out, hibernates, and renews. They also display a fluidity when it comes to genre, discarding the potential restrictions within them by eschewing their conventions. Filmed in London, Pantheon wavers between altered and inner perceptions, and acts as an ode to nature. Beneath its surface, though, Pantheon takes in a lot more than nature. Its sixteen tracks are named after Goddesses and span multiple cultures and eras, and a femininity perfumes the soundscapes. Using samples from their own recordings produced, in their words, ‘something weathered…with the spirit of a well-loved cassette but using cutting edge production techniques’. The recordings evolve naturally, but they had a little help along the way. The process reflected ‘the cyclical and evolutionary nature of all creative processes’. Opening track ‘Flora’ features a warm, swelling harmony and a dapple of birdsong; morning is here, promising plenty. The track expands, the notes pouring out and overflowing. Bon’s unlimited horizons are evident right from the start. Unafraid to push into bold new areas of sound while retaining its ambient and modern classical aesthetic, Pantheon is not your typical album. Its fresh, expansive sound is ready to shatter any preconceived notions of what one might expect. The lower register of the strings seem to provide the gravel, the dirt, within the music, while on a microscopic level, soft, chiming notes seem to indicate cool raindrops, or a scattering of morning dew. Noise, gentle hiss, and distortion are intentional and vital elements to the music, so much so that they’re treated as instruments in their own right. The pair look to explore the question: what is quality, perfection, and character, and what do these words mean to us? ?On Pantheon, Bon are also joined by Laraaji, Maxwell Sterling, and Lucinda Chua, and the expanse furthers even more with the addition of these artists. The album is a natural wonder, gently unfolding and glowing as it does so. Just like the natural world, music can’t be rushed. It has its own time and place – its own season – and Bon develop the peach-sweet sound with patience, not necessarily directly affecting the resulting music, as it seems to grow on its own, developing branches and roots over time. Pantheon by BON www.spatialawareness.com
items._genre: ambient / modern classical / experimental electronic / neo-classical
items._cn_summary: Bon是由Yerosha Windrich与Alex Morris组成的双人组合，专辑《Pantheon》以十六首曲目对应不同文化与时代中的女神形象。整体音乐带有环境音乐与现代古典的交融特质，开篇曲目以温暖和声与鸟鸣采样展开，弦乐低频铺垫如泥土与碎石般厚实，高频细碎的钟声模拟雨滴与晨露。噪音、磁带嘶声与失真被刻意保留并作为乐器本身来使用，营造出'被时间打磨过的磁带'质感。制作上既使用前沿技术也保留原始录音的粗粝，呈现循环演进的有机生长过程。专辑还邀请了Laraaji、Maxwell Sterling与Lucinda Chua参与，扩展了声音的广度与层次。整张作品将自然意象、女性气质与跨文化神话融为一体，以季节更迭的节奏缓慢展开。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这是一张聚焦圣多美和普林西比（非洲最小的葡语国家之一）70至80年代Puxa舞曲的合辑，属于该系列第二卷。Puxa是一种融合了前葡属非洲殖民地音乐元素的复合风格，吸收了merengue、Soukouss、Benga等多种节奏，被认为具有召唤或驱赶灵体的仪式功能。葡萄牙殖民者曾试图禁止Puxa舞蹈但未能成功。专辑中Pedro Lima领衔的乐队展示了闷音吉他与鼓组的激烈对话，Sangazuza等曲目则展现了当贝斯与键盘退出后，鼓与吉他如何驱动舞者进入狂热状态。多把吉他交织盘旋，主唱与和声互为呼应，节奏悠长延展，适合长时间现场演奏。尽管录音有限，这批音乐呈现了两个岛屿独特的音乐面貌，体现了PALOP（葡语非洲国家）地区的文化交融。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由Analog Africa厂牌发行，聚焦贝宁传奇乐队Orchestre Poly-Rythmo与歌手兼作曲家Antoine Dougbé在1977至1982年间的合作。Dougbé以拍击大腿演绎Cavacha节奏著称，这一律动由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车节拍中提炼而来，后席卷70年代中期的刚果流行乐。作为伏都教实践者，Dougbé只与Poly-Rythmo合作，认为唯有他们能精准呈现其音乐构想。乐评指出，专辑音色调制带有80年代初的塑料光泽与合成器介入，但根基仍扎在70年代。开篇曲目明显受古巴son影响，反复出现的牛铃、鼻音式呼应唱腔构成典型段落；'Ma Won Min Towe Leo'以合成器铺底，干瘪的吉他音色在高帽驱动的律动中交织展开。整体呈现非洲传统节奏、古巴影响与刚果伦巴在录音技术变迁中的交汇，是研究西非流行音乐跨文化流动的重要文本。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自挪威Camilla Hole Trio，是他们此前科幻合成器与民间素材结合的探索之后，回归更具大地根基的一张作品。高音萨克斯手Camilla Hole与贝斯手Egil Kalman、鼓手兼颤音琴手Knut Kvifte Nesheim组成的三人组，在角色分配上刻意模糊，旋律与节奏在成员之间不断流转。开场曲取自挪威西部传统的Springleik舞曲，先由萨克斯陈述旋律，叠加模块合成器与颤音琴的色彩后逐渐转为即兴展开，最终以主题回归收束。整张专辑延续了超越本国民间音乐边界的追求，将传统素材、自由即兴与电子声响编织在一起，乐评聚焦于其灵活的互动结构与跨类型融合的处理方式。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴家与挪威音乐家父子组成的三重奏演绎，主要素材来自两国传统舞曲，却被处理成类似室内乐的三人对话。小提琴、竖笛（包括萨克斯与风袋等非传统乐器）与鼓的组合模糊了民间音乐与学院音乐之间的界限，乐评指出其不适合舞蹈伴奏，而更倾向于挖掘旋律背后的隐秘意味与暗流。评论以挪威塞特斯达尔河谷的"瀑布精灵"传说开场，强调斯堪的纳维亚舞曲表层欢乐之下潜藏的不安与阴暗。乐评将音乐比作易卜生戏剧中表面融洽实则暗藏危机的人际张力，整张专辑呈现一种对传统素材的非传统解读，既保持旋律根基又以碎片化、纹理化的方式重新构建。

items.album: Dizzy Scent Summons Spectral Folk on Her New EP “Doggy’s Cake”
items.excerpt: An acoustic guitar can make a room feel inhabited; on Dizzy Scent’s Doggy’s Cake, it also makes you wonder what else might be in there. Fingers travel audibly across strings, gentle strumming takes on the unease of branches brushing a house after dark, and a voice slips between a confidential murmur and a disorienting chorus. Across these six songs, familiar folk gestures acquire strange proportions, with tenderness, sensuality, and distress sharing the same small space. Released on September 11
items.body: An acoustic guitar can make a room feel inhabited; on Dizzy Scent’s Doggy’s Cake, it also makes you wonder what else might be in there. Fingers travel audibly across strings, gentle strumming takes on the unease of branches brushing a house after dark, and a voice slips between a confidential murmur and a disorienting chorus. Across these six songs, familiar folk gestures acquire strange proportions, with tenderness, sensuality, and distress sharing the same small space. Released on September 11, 2026, Doggy’s Cake follows July’s debut album, My Polarizing Nature, from independent singer, songwriter, and guitarist Dizzy Scent. She describes her approach as “dark raw,” pursuing instinctive playing and unusual chords while managing her career herself. In her account of the EP’s creation, depression, occult interests, and frustration with the music industry all feed into the work. Her attachment to imperfection comes with a pointed explanation: “Imperfection has a greater impact on humans because, with perfection, we already know what to expect.” That philosophy suits a record in which the movement of a hand across strings and an unguarded vocal sound carry so much feeling. The relationship between guitar and singer stays exposed, allowing changes in delivery to alter the character of an entire passage. The EP’s first track, “Witch (When Im Completely Red)” opens with acoustic strumming that scratches like the branches of a skeletal old tree against the side of a house at night. Over that dry contact, her soft, ghostly vocals develop a folky flutter, then climb into high notes resembling wind whistling around the building. There is something eerie and otherworldly about the way those two elements occupy the same space: the guitar feels close and physical, while the singing seems to drift beyond its reach. At nearly seven minutes, the opener gives that sensation ample time to develop. Dizzy’s release notes connect the song to her fascination with magic and admiration for Papus, placing its supernatural associations within her broader occult interests. The gently strummed opening of “My Dark Sides” has the plain, soothing shape of a lullaby. Her voice enters in a hushed whisper, suggesting an incantation murmured quietly enough to be mistaken for someone talking to herself. As the singing quivers and flutters, higher notes take on the character of a cry carried by the wind. The effect suggests glimpses of an inner world projected into the room, with the simplicity of the guitar making every vocal tremor more conspicuous. Dizzy describes the song as an effort to free herself from fears and the darker aspects of her character; the tentative intimacy of the performance gives those concerns a fragile, immediate presence. “Unchangeable” pushes the guitar forward with deep, resonant tones, its volume drawing attention to the sound of fingers gliding along the strings. Her singing carries a smoldering sensuality, almost jazzy in character, while retaining its folky appeal. A dreamy, ethereal quality surrounds that tactile opening. Halfway through, the arrangement becomes pleasingly unruly, resembling a chorus of ghostly voices, and her singing climbs higher while preserving its silky texture. The shortest song on the EP packs considerable movement into its two and a half minutes. According to Dizzy, it grew from months of searching for recognition and fielding opinions about her music before finding someone who acknowledged its value. She remains attached to the unusual chords and imperfections that make the work hers. Soft guitar strumming moves through “So That Means To Be An Artist And Sing ?” like footsteps on a moonlit walk. Dizzy’s languid, smoky delivery recalls PJ Harvey, its sensuality carried by the ease with which her voice drifts into the song. Around the one-minute mark, the arrangement and layered vocals become ghostly and disorienting for nearly a minute. A spoken turn and a grunt of pain follow that passage, before the folky singing returns and the sequence begins again. These changes give the performance an unstable emotional temperature, passing from languor through confusion to an abrupt expression of hurt. The title also echoes the question about being an artist raised in her accompanying statement, which criticizes the glamour and hypocrisy she associates with the music industry. More of the room is audible on “Blood Everywhere.” Ambient tone surrounds deliberate guitar strumming and a simple melody, while Dizzy’s vocals remain eerily hushed and murmured. Rattling sounds enter later, introducing small disturbances around the subdued performance. With so much space audible around the guitar and voice, those noises become unusually noticeable. The song’s unease rests in that exposed setting, where a quiet rattle can feel as consequential as a raised voice. A dog barks at the opening of “Life Is A Dog,” before gentle guitar strumming accompanies bluesy, folky singing. Her lamenting delivery carries a deep sorrow, with eerie layers of reverberant vocals gathering around it. Midway through, the song pauses for a spectral vocal passage, distorted and unstable like a voice breaking up on the radio or a cassette warbling as it plays. The interruption is chilling, briefly displacing the familiar intimacy of guitar and singer. When the earlier strumming and vocal style resume, that sorrow remains central. In her release notes, Dizzy links the song to anger toward the world and the suffering she has endured; the lament in her delivery gives those stated concerns an aching musical form. The EP takes its name from that closing song’s premise: life is a dog, and the cake is a piece of herself offered in response. Across the record, the guitar’s simplicity leaves room for a remarkably changeable voice, capable of moving from a folky murmur to bluesy complaint, sensual ease, or something suddenly strange and difficult to place. Her most unsettling passages grow from alterations to that intimate relationship, making the return of a familiar vocal tone feel newly significant. Dizzy makes her preference clear: “I love amateur art. It’s the most beautiful.” Her defense of instinctive expression runs alongside a wish to reach other people living with depression, a purpose she explains in the release statement. That desire for connection gives a generous dimension to her forceful insistence on doing things her own way: “Whether you believe in me or not, I don’t care. Because I believe in myself and my guitar. Fuck the rest.” Doggy’s Cake is out now digitally, with vinyl and CD editions available through ElasticStage. Order the EP here. Follow Dizzy Scent: Instagram YouTube TikTok The post Dizzy Scent Summons Spectral Folk on Her New EP “Doggy’s Cake” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张以原声吉他为核心的六首作品EP，延续了独立创作人Dizzy Scent首张专辑的暗黑质感。整张唱片围绕'不完美'的美学展开，手指在琴弦上的摩擦声、裸露的低语式人声与空旷的和弦走向共同营造出不安而亲密的氛围。评论者多次将吉他摩擦比作深夜树枝刮过房屋外墙，将高音演唱比作风声，形成物理性乐器与超脱声线之间的张力。创作背景涉及抑郁情绪、神秘学兴趣与对音乐工业的挫败感，作品将民谣的熟悉手势赋予扭曲的比例，使温柔、感官性与痛苦共享同一狭小空间。原声编制中偶尔透出爵士化的感性唱腔，声乐颤动被放大为内在世界的投射。整体气质介于民谣根性与暗潮氛围之间，以极简手段承载了丰富的情绪层次。

Another ghost. Another shadow. Another thought. Another possibility. Another door. Another doorway behind the door. “Another” is a fitting word attached to a record that rarely stays where you expect it to. Cursed Frame is an album full of thresholds: sounds coming from across the room, voices emerging from the fog, something moving beneath the surface. items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — France has always been a land of revolutions, ranging from the political to the musical. The French had their own way of assimilating various foreign currents, adapting them to their own unique character. They did this with classic jazz, featuring musicians such as Michel Legrand, St�phane Grappelli, and Django Reinhardt (who, despite being Belgian, spent the majority of his career in France), and later by adopting jazz-rock fusion into their style, as exemplified by Jean-Luc Chevalier, a guitarist born in the Cholet region of France in 1948. In fact, Magma, Christian Vander's band, incorporated numerous fusion elements and featured Chevalier from 1978 to 1984.When he joined Magma, everything clicked perfectly; it wasn't just a matter of the style suiting his own. As Chevalier himself often maintained, what mattered was the "spirit," not pretentious intellectualism. He would often say that a track like John McLaughlin's "Guardian Angel" must have been composed in a trance-like state, driven by the energy of the moment. Chevalier used to say that Jeff Beck, Jaco Pastorius, Christian Vander, and Hendrix were not "armchair intellectuals," and that, precisely for this reason, that kind of contamination did not exist in Magma.With Magma, he played not only the guitar but also the bass, and, as he himself maintained, it was about intense emotions, about unleashing a hidden madness. He maintained a long-standing relationship, spanning many years, with percussionist Jean Chevalier (known as "Popoff"), who had joined Zig Zag in 1972 and with whom he would form various duos and trios. In the early 1980s, he formally launched his solo career, performing in a trio alongside Bertrand Renaudin and Marc Eliard for the album Un pied dans le vide (1985), a work that featured an experimental vibe reminiscent of Mike Stern's early period (wild and fast-paced), as well as an ethnic spirit that permeated the recording.Paradoxe N�II calls to mind the pyrotechnic John McLaughlin of the pre-Mahavishnu era, when?even within the seemingly stripped-down jazz trio format, the sound could feel as though it were floating in space. Meanwhile, on L'Abandon, the guitar doubles the very same keyboard riffs typical of jazz fusion. Amiti�s et encore builds a melody, and in this regard, it also draws a parallel to Pat Metheny, who could improvise and experiment without ever losing sight of the harmonic and melodic direction."Baillou Pack Pack" features the electric bass driving a distinctly funk-oriented sound, while Chevalier's guitar work, incorporating distinctly Arabic-style solos, lends itself to extended improvisation; the track then shifts into a rock style, undergoing a dramatic stylistic metamorphosis, all within a single song.In "Concerto Grosso," percussion plays a pivotal role, and the nylon-string guitar provides a warm tone reminiscent of Baden Powell, who was living in Europe at the time, occasionally veering into dissonance and pushing boundaries in the same spirit as the Brazilian master."L'abrozo" continues the fusion with a highly recognizable bassline but a restless guitar, initially adopting a Robert Fripp-esque "Frippertronics" style before shifting into atmospheric jazz that the guitarist himself proceeds to distort, all while the rhythm section accelerates and decelerates in support. In any case, it's impossible not to tap your feet."Un pied dans le vide", the title track, appears at the end for a very good reason: it is epic. The melody is unusual for a fusion album; indeed, coming from a French guitarist schooled by Christian Vander, nothing could be predictable. Infernal, dark notes erupt from the guitar, while the drums and bass provide the wind that allows that "bird", his guitar, to take flight. There are echoes of King Crimson, uncommon for a fusion record, and one might even be reminded of the band Present, until a sophisticated atmosphere reminiscent of a French police procedural or film noir takes over the song, maintaining that same sense of mystery.During his time with Magma, Chevalier adopted the name Wurd Gorgo (in the style of Gong members) which meant something akin to "The Demon Gorgo" in Koba�an mythology. In doing so, he delved into the unfathomable depths of the spirit of his discography, inviting us to join him in that journey.
items._genre: jazz fusion / jazz-rock / experimental fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张1985年的专辑由法国吉他手Jean-Luc Chevalier领衔，延续了他在Magma乐队时期形成的融合美学。整体以爵士三重奏为核心框架，却在器乐编排与即兴走向上呈现出强烈的实验性。《Paradoxe NºII》展现了纯熟的速度型fusion吉他语汇，接近早年Mike Stern与McLaughlin的爆发力；《L'Abandon》以键盘为骨架，吉他叠加复调线条。《Baillou Pack Pack》是全辑最具色彩的一首，从funk节奏出发滑入阿拉伯风格独奏，再转入摇滚段落，单曲之内完成多次风格蜕变。《Concerto Grosso》转向尼龙弦吉他，呼应Baden Powell的温暖音色，同时引入打击乐主导与不和谐音程的张力。整张专辑兼具即兴的狂野与世界音乐色彩，体现出法国乐手将外来风格内化后再造的独特路径。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the major players of the 21st century folk revival scene, JOANNA NEWSOM has foundinternational fame with her unique musical performances that includes intricate harp instrumentationand a very unusual quirky vocal style. While her album "Ys" would propel to folk royalty, her debutrelease THE MILK-EYED MENDER was met with positive critique and universal love as well. NEWSOM grewup in Grass Valley, California and is actually distantly related to the state's governor. NEWSOM wasgifted with a rather quick ascent to fame after only appearing as a guest musician on a Nervous Copalbum before setting out on her own and capturing the folk world's attention in record time. After acouple warmup EPs, she has released four critically acclaimed albums so far.THE MILK-EYED MENDER was NEWSOM's debut which not only showcased her multi-instrumental talents thatincluded harpsichord, piano, keyboards and harp but also featured her unique songwriting styles thathad one foot in the catchy world of pop music while maintaining an authentic medieval feel detachedfrom the modern day excesses of production and technology overload. This is a solo album frombeginning to end with NEWSOM performing every instrumental and having written and sung every song.While "Ys" would evolve NEWSOM's sound into a more complex orchestral production, THE MILK-EYEDMENDER is the perfect place to inure your musical sensibilities to NEWSOM's bizarre sounding vocalidiosyncrasies.The album features 12 tracks that add up to just over 52 minutes and all written by NEWSOM herselfexcept the traditional folk song "Three Little Babies." The album indeed comes off as a collectionof child-like songs structured around the harp which plays an interesting role as both the basis forrhythm as well as providing the melodic backing to NEWSOM's lyrical performances. The album alsofeatures both acoustic and electric pianos as well as harpsichord but the album is fairly sparse asfar as instrumentation and showcases NEWSOM's ability to express herself through the barest of bonessimplicity and yet sounding somehow uncannily complete with the harp alone serving as the entireinstrumentation for the majority of the album's run.While the most stripped down and most accessible of NEWSOM's releases that would become moreexperimental after this one's release, THE MILK-EYED MENDER holds up as a well-constructed piece ofharp-based folk music in its own right despite no excursions into the progressive chamber folk thatwould find her embraced by the modern New Weird America culture that found NEWSOM in the company ofthe likes of Devendra Barnhart, Animal Collective and Espers. Ironically this strong debut wouldprove to only be the beginning for NEWSOM who quickly captured the momentum and expanded herambitions into the world of more complex progressive arenas. Many may find this a bit too naive andinnocent in comparison to the grandiosity of "Ys" however it's exactly the bare bones authenticitythat i find appealing about this debut which establishes NEWSOM as a talent in her own right beforegoing into more adventurous collaborative efforts.
items._genre: prog folk / harp folk / medieval-influenced
items._cn_summary: 这张处女作以竖琴为绝对主导，乔安娜·纽森独自包揽所有乐器与人声，营造出近乎中世纪民谣的质朴氛围。专辑收录十二首作品，仅一首为传统民谣，其余皆为原创，歌词具有童话般的叙事色彩。编曲上刻意保持稀疏，竖琴同时承担节奏骨架与旋律走向，辅以原声钢琴、电钢琴与羽管键琴点缀，整体呈现一种剥离现代制作冗余的素净感。相比后来与管弦乐团合作的《Ys》，本作更易接近，但已展现出她独特的声线特质与跨类型语汇——一只手伸向流行旋律的抓耳，另一只手则探向古老民谣的源头。作为进步民谣与新世纪奇异美学的桥梁之作，它为后续更实验化的探索奠定了根基。
